result.title: Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
result.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI), in which a system also improves the way it improves, is a long-standing aspiration on the path to AGI. Language agents increasingly store procedural knowledge in reusable skills. Optimizing skills offers a direct way to achieve RSI, because the optimization procedure itself can be encoded as a skill. Existing skill optimizers, however, follow a hand-designed procedure. Even methods that evolve a meta-skill confine it to a fixed pipeline and relearn it for each task. We present Skill$^{\infty}$, which makes skill optimization recursively self-improving: a meta agent follows a meta-skill to optimize task skills and optimizes the meta-skill itself using the same procedure. The optimization is agent-led. The meta agent diagnoses execution traces, proposes candidates, requests independent reviews, and allocates the search budget. The meta-skill defines these steps, allowing self-improvement to rewrite them. This meta-skill is also decoupled from task skills, refined on multiple skill optimization tasks and then reused to optimize task skills across diverse domains. As in deployment, skills at both levels are standard packages loaded through native skill discovery. On 83 SkillsBench tasks, Skill$^{\infty}$ reaches a pass rate of 60.7%, compared with 56.4% for human-curated skills and 54.5% for SkillEvolver.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Skill∞，让 meta agent 按一份可被自身重写的 meta-skill 去优化任务技能，实现「优化过程本身也被优化」的递归自我改进，并在 83 个 SkillsBench 任务上报告通过率提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「诊断执行轨迹—提出候选—独立评审—分配搜索预算」且可被重写的优化流程，可能为 LVR 中的轨迹监督、贡献分配与计算预算/停止决策提供可迁移线索，但该工作面向纯文本技能包，是否涉及内部状态或视觉证据需核查。
